19s düşündü

The key distinction is between withdrawn applications and formally denied applications. HMDA treats these as different outcomes, and denial rates should not include withdrawals in their denominator.

### 1\. National FHA application outcomes in 2025

The 2025 HMDA data were released by the CFPB on March 31, 2026. The underlying records are available through the [official CFPB/FFIEC HMDA data publication](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/about-us/newsroom/2025-hmda-data-on-mortgage-lending-now-available/). Consumer Financial Protection Bureau +1

For FHA applications reaching a credit decision:

FHA denial rate, 2025

### 22.1%

262,250 denied applications

EXACT DENOMINATOR

### 1,187,606

Applications reaching a credit decision

Calculation: 262,250 ÷ 1,187,606 = 22.1%.

The denominator includes:

* Action 1: Loan originated.

* Action 2: Approved but not accepted.

* Action 3: Denied.

It excludes:

* Action 4: Withdrawn by applicant.

* Action 5: Closed for incompleteness.

* Reverse mortgages (HECM).

Important qualification about withdrawals: The 22.1% figure does not tell us what percentage of all FHA applications were withdrawn. Withdrawals are expressly excluded from its denominator. I would not substitute a percentage of all applications for the requested withdrawal share without calculating the separate action-4 count from the complete HMDA file.

Source: [FinanceRateCalc – 2025 FHA denial analysis and denominator](https://financeratecalc.com/how-often-are-fha-loans-denied.html). Its methodology and correction history are published alongside the figures. FinanceRateCalc +1

### 2\. Pulte Mortgage's FHA denial rate and DTI reasons

PULTE MORTGAGE LLC · 2025 HMDA

### 26.8%

FHA denial rate

### 4,567

FHA applications

Pulte's overall FHA denial rate, calculated against applications reaching a credit decision, not all applications submitted.

Source: [Pulte Mortgage – 2025 HMDA lender data](https://lenderregister.com/lender/5493004wmln60zj2on46-pulte-mortgage-llc/).

The 26.8% rate is also reported by the independent lender-level analysis at [Mortgage Lender Rankings](https://mortgagelenderrankings.com/lender/pulte-mortgage). Lender Register +1

What about debt-to-income (DTI)?

There are two different statistics that should not be confused:

* Pulte's overall mortgage portfolio: 65.9% of denials had DTI as the first-listed reason.

* Pulte's FHA portfolio: the FHA-specific DTI share must be calculated using FHA denials only, rather than all Pulte denials.

The FHA-specific data published by Ground Figures break down DTI-related denials by DTI band:

| FHA DTI band | Denials citing DTI |
| ------------ | ------------------ |
| 43% or less  | 34%                |
| 44–45%       | 29%                |
| 46–49%       | 24%                |
| 50–60%       | 51%                |
| Above 60%    | 74%                |

These percentages are conditional on the DTI band, not percentages of all FHA denials. Ground Figures

I cannot substantiate a single aggregate percentage of Pulte's FHA denials citing DTI from the figures above, so I would not present the 65.9% all-product figure as the FHA figure.

The underlying records are available in the [HMDA data dictionary](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields) and the [2025 FHA denial-reason dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FinanceRateCalc/fha-denial-reason-fingerprints).

### 3\. What does ECOA adverse action code 18 mean?

There is an important coding distinction here.

HMDA's official denial-reason codes do not include code 18. The HMDA code for debt-to-income ratio is:

HMDA denial reason 1

Code 1 — Debt-to-income ratio.

It means the lender determined that the applicant's existing monthly obligations were excessive relative to income, or that income was insufficient for the amount of credit requested.

The official HMDA filing instructions explain this classification. HMDA Documentation +1

If your actual mortgage adverse-action notice says code 18, I would need to see the name of the lender or the coding legend accompanying the notice to establish its meaning. Code 18 is not a universally established ECOA denial-reason code.

Under Regulation B, creditors must provide specific reasons for adverse action, rather than merely saying that an application failed internal standards. See [CFPB Regulation B, §1002.9](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/9/). Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

### 4\. Is the FHA DTI limit a HUD rule or the lender's own threshold?

The answer is both, but in different senses: HUD provides underwriting guidelines, while lenders retain underwriting discretion.

Historically, FHA manual underwriting guidelines have used:

| Ratio                                                       | Traditional FHA guideline |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Housing expense / gross monthly income (front-end)          | 31%                       |
| Total monthly obligations / gross monthly income (back-end) | 43%                       |

These are commonly referred to as the 31/43 ratios.

However, exceeding these ratios does not automatically mean an FHA loan must be denied.

HUD's guidance allows higher ratios when the lender provides appropriate justification and compensating factors. Automated underwriting through the FHA TOTAL Scorecard also changes how these ratios are evaluated.

HUD's archived official reference guide explicitly states that exceeding the 31/43 ratios requires justification and compensating factors for applicable manual underwriting cases, while the requirement does not apply in the same way to loans receiving an acceptable TOTAL Scorecard result. archives.hud.gov

What this means in practice:

* HUD establishes FHA underwriting requirements and risk-assessment rules.

* A lender can apply stricter internal underwriting thresholds, often called lender overlays.

* A lender's refusal to approve a particular DTI does not necessarily mean HUD itself prohibits that DTI.

* A high DTI can still result in approval under an appropriate FHA underwriting pathway.

Pulte's 2025 data are particularly interesting in this context: its FHA approval figures show 85% approval in the 50–60% DTI band, but 0% approval above 60% in the reported purchase-loan sample. These are observed historical outcomes, not proof of Pulte's current written underwriting policy. Ground Figures

### Sources and interpretation

* [CFPB – 2025 HMDA data release](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/about-us/newsroom/2025-hmda-data-on-mortgage-lending-now-available/) — primary federal data source.

* [2025 FHA national denial analysis](https://financeratecalc.com/how-often-are-fha-loans-denied.html) — national denial count and exact denominator.

* [Pulte Mortgage 2025 HMDA data](https://lenderregister.com/lender/5493004wmln60zj2on46-pulte-mortgage-llc/) — FHA application volume and denial rate.

* [Ground Figures – Pulte Mortgage](https://groundfigures.com/lenders/pulte-mortgage/) — FHA denial outcomes by DTI band.

* [FFIEC HMDA Filing Instructions](https://ffiec.beta.cfpb.gov/documentation/fig/2026/overview) — official denial-reason codes.

* [HUD HOC Reference Guide](https://archives.hud.gov/offices/hsg/sfh/ref/sfhp2-12.cfm) — FHA DTI underwriting guidelines.

* [CFPB Regulation B, §1002.9](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/9/) — adverse-action notice requirements.

One detail worth resolving: If you can share the actual denial notice or tell me which lender issued the notice containing code 18, I can identify the applicable code definition rather than assume it is a federal ECOA code.
